# CHAPTER ONE: Phytoplankton Ecology

## Phytoplankton: Primary Producers

::::: columns
::: {.column width="40%"}
**Definition:** Microscopic photoautotrophic organisms forming the foundation of aquatic food webs

**Systematic Characteristics:** 
- Unicellular to colonial algae
- Contain chlorophyll-a (Chl-a) for photosynthesis
- Osmotic regulation through passive transport
- Confined to photic zone (depth-dependent)

:::

::: {.column width="60%"}

```{r}
knitr::include_graphics("images/what is phyto/What_phyto.png")
```

*Diverse phytoplankton taxa: diatoms, dinoflagellates, coccolithophores*

:::
:::::

## Ecological Significance

:::::: columns
::: {.column width="60%"}
**Net Primary Production (NPP):**

-   Phytoplankton contribute ~50% of global marine NPP
-   Fix inorganic carbon through photosynthesis
-   Produce dissolved oxygen through oxygenic photosynthesis

**Trophic Dynamics:**

-   Base of planktonic food webs
-   Energy transfer to zooplankton and larval fish
-   Support of pelagic and demersal fisheries

-   **Biogeochemical Cycling:**
    -   Carbon sequestration in deep ocean
    -   Regeneration of macro- and micronutrients
    -   Participation in silicon and nitrogen cycles
:::

:::: {.column width="40%"}
::: callout-warning
## Ecosystem Implications

Phytoplankton biomass perturbations result in:

- Altered energy flow efficiency
- Food web restructuring
- Disrupted elemental cycling
- Trophic cascades to higher predators
:::
